executiveSummary.oneLiner: Hermes is a full-stack, end-to-end encrypted real-time messaging platform supporting private and group chat, deployed on a self-managed k3s Kubernetes cluster on GCP — built, provisioned, and automated entirely from scratch.
executiveSummary.problemStatement: Build a self-hosted, production-deployable chat system that solves the full engineering stack: real-time communication, cryptographic privacy, multi-tenant authentication, cloud infrastructure, container orchestration, automated CI/CD, and observability — without relying on managed services.
executiveSummary.solutionOverview: A Spring Boot backend provides REST APIs for authentication and data access, and WebSocket/STOMP for real-time messaging. End-to-end encryption is implemented client-side via the WebCrypto API — the server never sees plaintext private message content. Infrastructure is provisioned via Terraform and Ansible onto GCP, orchestrated with k3s Kubernetes, and deployed through a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline with Trivy security scanning.
primaryUsers: Registered end users requiring private, secure, real-time communication
keyCapabilities: End-to-end encryption — ECDH P-256 key exchange, AES-GCM per-message encryption via WebCrypto API
Real-time private and group messaging via WebSocket/STOMP over SockJS
Google OAuth2 + email/password authentication with OTP email verification and password reset
JWT access + refresh token lifecycle with secure cookie storage
File and image sharing with Redis image caching
Live user presence and typing indicators
Per-user Redis rate limiting with sliding window algorithm
Group creation, membership management, and group-scoped messaging
Kubernetes-deployed: Deployments, StatefulSets, HPA, NetworkPolicies, CronJob, cert-manager
GitHub Actions CI/CD with Trivy security scanning and smoke testing
Prometheus + Grafana observability stack
knownLimitations: In-memory STOMP broker does not scale horizontally — RabbitMQ externalisation is on the roadmap
Local file storage is not persistent across pod restarts
Message history limited to last 24 hours

architecture.overview: React/Vite SPA communicates with a Spring Boot monolith via REST and WebSocket/STOMP. E2EE is handled client-side using WebCrypto API before messages reach the server. Infrastructure is two GCP VMs running a k3s cluster, provisioned via Terraform and configured via Ansible. CI/CD is fully automated through GitHub Actions.

architecture.architectureRationale: WebSocket/STOMP enables low-latency chat while REST handles authentication and data retrieval. Client-side E2EE ensures server compromise does not expose private message content. Terraform + Ansible + k3s provides reproducible infrastructure without managed service lock-in. In-memory STOMP broker is the known horizontal scaling bottleneck — RabbitMQ externalisation resolves it when needed.

executiveSummary.oneLiner: Pokeverse is a real-time multiplayer game platform providing shared infrastructure — authentication, room lifecycle, WebSocket event routing, chat, and state management — so individual game types can plug in without re-solving those problems each time.
executiveSummary.problemStatement: Every multiplayer game requires the same solved problems: player authentication, room creation and lifecycle management, real-time event distribution, chat, and persistent state. Building them from scratch every time is wasteful and produces inconsistent quality. Pokeverse centralises these into a reusable platform.
executiveSummary.solutionOverview: A Spring Boot platform backend exposes shared services for authentication, room management, real-time messaging via WebSocket/STOMP, and persistence. Individual game types plug in as modules and consume these services. A Pokémon Quiz game — supporting single-player and multiplayer modes — demonstrates the platform with room-scoped STOMP broadcasting and live session scoring. PostgreSQL handles durable persistence; Redis handles hot-path game state.
primaryUsers: Hosts creating and managing multiplayer rooms
Administrators managing game content (RBAC on roadmap)
keyCapabilities: Centralised OAuth2 authentication with JWT access and refresh tokens
Reusable room creation, join/leave lifecycle, and session management
Real-time events via WebSocket/STOMP — topic-based and queue-based routing
Shared in-room chat system with persistence
Pluggable game module architecture — stable platform concerns separated from game-specific logic
Dual data store: PostgreSQL 17 (Flyway-managed) for durable state, Redis 7 for low-latency active session data
Pokémon Quiz: single-player with session tracking and analysis; multiplayer with room-scoped live gameplay
knownLimitations: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) is not implemented; admin access is currently handled via request parameters
Only one game module (Pokémon Quiz) is currently implemented
No Kubernetes deployment yet — Docker Compose for local dev

architecture.overview: A Next.js frontend communicates with a Spring Boot game platform via REST and WebSocket/STOMP. The platform exposes shared services for authentication, rooms, messaging, and persistence, while individual games reuse these services and implement only their game-specific logic. PostgreSQL 17 with Flyway stores durable data; Redis 7 handles fast state access for active game sessions.

architecture.architectureRationale: The platform/module separation keeps stable concerns (auth, rooms, messaging, persistence) decoupled from game-specific logic, enabling new game types to be added without re-implementing infrastructure. Flyway-managed schema over ddl-auto=update ensures forward-only migrations safe for production. Redis vs PostgreSQL split is intentional: durable game history goes to PostgreSQL; transient active state that changes every few seconds stays in Redis.

executiveSummary.oneLiner: A scientific expression evaluator built from scratch using classic compiler techniques — tokenisation, implicit multiplication injection, Shunting-Yard postfix conversion, and stack-based evaluation. Supporting 50+ mathematical functions and 70+ operators with zero external math dependencies.
executiveSummary.problemStatement: Most calculator projects call eval() or a library. This project explores how calculators and programming language parsers actually work: what happens between the user typing '2 + 3 * sin(pi/4)^2' and a number appearing on screen?
executiveSummary.solutionOverview: A Python package exposes a StackQueueCalculator that tokenises input, injects implicit multiplication, converts to postfix via the Shunting-Yard algorithm, and evaluates results with a function registry covering arithmetic, trig, hyperbolic, logs, combinatorics, and constants. A Medium article explains the algorithm and implementation decisions publicly.
primaryUsers: Developers and learners exploring parsing algorithms and DSA concepts
Students studying compiler techniques and stack-based evaluation
Developers wanting a programmable scientific calculator library
keyCapabilities: Expression tokenisation with implicit multiplication injection ('2pi' → '2 * pi')
Shunting-Yard algorithm for infix-to-postfix conversion with full precedence and associativity
Stack-based postfix (RPN) evaluation
50+ functions: arithmetic, trig, hyperbolic, logarithms, combinatorics (nPr, nCr, GCD, LCM), utility (abs, floor, ceil, hypot, atan2)
5 constants (π, e, τ, φ, ans), memory operations (M+, M-, MR, MC), and last-answer reference
Domain validation (no sqrt of negative, no division by zero) and overflow protection
100+ test cases across 9 categories
Zero external math library dependencies
knownLimitations: No CLI or GUI interface — usage is via Python API
No persistence layer for history or memory across runs
No complex-number support for invalid domains (e.g., sqrt(-1))

architecture.overview: A single-process Python library where expression processing flows through a linear pipeline: tokeniser → implicit multiplication injector → postfix converter → stack evaluator. Math function groups are modularised by domain (trig, hyperbolic, math) in a function registry. The StackQueueCalculator orchestrates the pipeline and maintains in-process memory and last-answer state.

components.name: StackQueueCalculator
responsibilities: Orchestrate tokenisation, postfix conversion, and stack evaluation
Maintain in-process memory and last-answer state
Register functions and constants into the function registry

components.name: Tokenizer
responsibilities: Convert input string to typed tokens (numbers, operators, functions, constants)
Distinguish unary negation from binary subtraction
Identify named constants and function calls

components.name: Implicit Multiplication Injector
responsibilities: Insert missing * tokens without introducing ambiguity ('2pi' → '2 * pi', '2(3+4)' → '2 * (3+4)')

components.name: Postfix Converter
responsibilities: Apply Shunting-Yard algorithm to convert infix to RPN
Respect operator precedence and associativity
Handle parentheses, unary functions, and binary functions

components.name: Postfix Evaluator
responsibilities: Evaluate postfix expression via operand stack operations
Dispatch to function registry for named unary and binary functions
Domain validation and overflow protection

components.name: Function Modules
responsibilities: Provide math, trig, and hyperbolic function implementations
Safe domain validation checks for all 50+ functions
Combinatorics with overflow protection (factorial of large numbers)

steps: User passes an expression string to evaluate()
Tokeniser converts string into typed tokens
Implicit multiplication injector inserts missing * operators
Postfix converter applies Shunting-Yard and generates RPN sequence
Stack evaluator computes final numeric result with domain validation
User calls memory add/subtract/recall/clear
Calculator updates in-process memory state
Memory value available as operand in subsequent expressions

architecture.architectureRationale: The tokeniser → Shunting-Yard → postfix evaluation pipeline mirrors classic compiler front-end structure, keeping each stage's responsibility clear and independently testable. Zero external math dependencies keeps the project self-contained and the implementation educational — there is no abstraction hiding how it actually works.
